page: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-8GB is an entry-level virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate modest performance characteristics. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks fall into the weak category, representing the bottom 25%. However, the server achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside an average Geekbench single-core score. Multi-threaded operations, such as Geekbench multi-core and bzip3 decompression, drop to weak or poor tiers due to the shared resource model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU architecture and lack of bundled local storage position this server as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained high-performance compute. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, development and testing environments, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving where resource demands are intermittent.
